newsitem.title: USA: AIG second-quarter net rises as premiums grow.
newsitem.headline: AIG second-quarter net rises as premiums grow.

text.p: Insurance carrier American International Group Inc. Thursday reported higher earnings for the second quarter amid growth in worldwide general insurance premiums.
"AIG had a very satisfactory quarter, with solid performance from all of our principal businesses," said AIG Chairman M.R. Greenberg.

"In general insurance, worldwide net premiums written before the impact of foreign exchange rose 7.5 percent from last year's second quarter. We achieved an underwriting profit of $134.5 million and a combined ratio of 95.92," he said in a statement accompanying the results.
Earnings for the quarter rose to $826.5 million, or $1.77 a share, from $724.4 million, or $1.53 a share, a year earlier.
AIG said worldwide life insurance net premiums rose 13 percent after the impact of foreign exchange.
Before the foreign exchange impact, worldwide life insurance net premiums rose 17.5 percent.
"Our life operations in Asia, Central Europe and Latin America all reported strong results," Greenberg said.
"Life operations in Russia have commenced, and we recently received a license to operate a wholly owned life company in Uruguay," he added.

In the United States, AIG's growing life insurance business continued to report strong results. Life insurance premium income rose 13.0 percent in the second quarter to $2.55 billion from $2.25 billion in 1996, AIG said.
In financial services, second-quarter pretax operating income rose 30.8 percent to $173.6 million, compared with $132.7 million in 1996, AIG said.
In Japan, AIG's joint venture with Mitsubishi Trust and Banking Corp. in investment management, announced earlier this year, became fully licensed in the quarter.
AIG continued its programme to repurchase shares of its common stock in the open market. For the six months ended June 30, AIG said, it repurchased approximately 2.3 million shares.

"Underwriting results were satisfactory, as we continued to focus on our core speciality products and remained disciplined in not seeking to build business in areas that fail to meet our underwriting standards," Greenberg said.
Workers' compensation rates, in particular, have continued to fall to unacceptable levels in a number of states, Greenberg said.
AIG's stock was down $2 at $150.875 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
